$comment: THIS VIDEO: one entry per scene, in order. text = what the voice says (spell names the way they're said). cues = name → the spoken word that fires it (first match; numbers match as digits or words). captionPhrases = spoken phrase → how captions show it. The last scene may be overlay: true (drawn over the pulled-back world). Optional: voice = { provider, <provider>: { ...settings } } to override the repo config for this video (paid voices still need npm run voice -- --final); music = { file (in public/), volume, duck } for a bed that dips under the voice (make one with: node ../bin/posthouse.mjs asset music "prompt" --seconds N --name bed); commercial: true to check licences for paid use; sting: false to drop the sign-off sound. The example is examples/hello-posthouse/post.md.

scenes.text: You wrote a great post. Most people will scroll right past it. But they'll stop for a video.
Post house reads your post and writes a short script. One idea per scene, and every number comes straight from your words.
Then a voice reads it. Use ElevenLabs, a free voice that runs on your own machine, or no voice at all.
Every word gets a timestamp, so the picture moves at the exact moment the voice says it.
And there are no slides. One camera glides across a single stage, carrying each idea into the next.
Point it at a post, and get a video back. Post house is free and open source, on GitHub.
